title: "I was completely overwhelmed..."
caption: The Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds and airglow over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way arches over one of the Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope, with the two Magellanic Clouds beside it. Along the horizon runs a faint green and red shimmer of airglow, light the atmosphere gives off by itself and that shows only under very dark skies. To the left, the zodiacal light rises like a white brushstroke.

French astrophotographer Julien Looten made this 360-degree panorama during a visit to the VLT at Cerro Paranal in Chile, a place with one of the darkest skies on Earth. One of the VLT's Unit Telescopes adds laser beams to the scene. They help correct the blurring caused by turbulence in the atmosphere.

Looten comes from northern France, where cloud and light pollution often spoil the sky. He described being so overwhelmed by the view that he forgot everything around him, with the galactic bulge shining straight overhead. He called the night one of the most beautiful of his life.

understand.summary: This is a 360-degree panoramic landscape photograph by Julien Looten. The source gives no details of camera settings or color processing.
understand.eye: Airglow shows only under very dark skies, and the source does not say how the photograph's colors compare with the naked-eye view.
